about: Joule's catalogue of Predbat's Home Assistant settings. Each description is a short paraphrase of the cited section of Predbat's documentation at docsRef; it is left blank where the docs don't describe the setting. Defaults and units come from Predbat's CONFIG_ITEMS at the same ref. kind: tunable (a plan setting Joule may suggest, trial and restore), override (manual one-off controls), software (updates and save/restore), control (mode, read-only, calculating flag) or debug (diagnostics, notifications and Predbat-maintained values). Risk is Joule's own judgement: Low, Medium (shown as 'Needs care') or High. Keys ending _1.._7 reuse their base entry (cars and inverters 2-8).

settings.description: Share of energy assumed lost when charging the battery, as a decimal (0.03 means 3%).
Share of energy assumed lost when discharging the battery, as a decimal (0.03 means 3%).
Share of energy assumed lost converting between DC and AC in the inverter, as a decimal (0.04 means 4%).
On for a hybrid inverter, so solar charging the battery skips the inverter loss. Turn off for an AC-coupled battery.
Multiplies the maximum charge rate the inverter reports; 0.95 models charging 5% slower than reported.
Multiplies the maximum discharge rate the inverter reports; the default 1.05 models discharging 5% faster than reported.

settings.friendlyName: Charge rate in the cloudy (PV10) case
settings.description: Charge-rate factor used only in the pessimistic PV10% scenario; 0.8 assumes the battery charges at 80% of its normal rate. It doesn't change what is sent to the inverter.
Uses GivTCP's nominal battery capacity as the battery size instead of the reported capacity. Try it if your battery size is reported wrongly.
The lowest charge level kept in the battery; at this level the house runs from the grid. Predbat doesn't plan charging to reach a raised reserve.
A soft minimum battery level (kWh) for longer-term planning. It is ignored for the next 4 hours, so the battery can still drop below it; 0 uses the whole battery.
How strongly the plan stays above the keep level, even at extra cost. 0 ignores it; the default 0.5 is recommended.
Minimum level (kWh) for every charge slot and forced export. A non-zero value can make Predbat charge far more often unless the cheap-rate threshold limits it.
Caps how far each charge slot fills the battery (kWh); 0 turns the cap off. A cap can push charging or grid use into expensive periods.
A virtual cost per kWh charged and discharged, used only when planning, to reduce battery cycling. Around 0-2p is suggested; it isn't added to Predbat's reported costs.

settings.friendlyName: Value of energy left in the battery
settings.description: Scales what energy left in the battery at the end of the plan is worth. Below 1.0 values it less, above 1.0 holds more charge. Lowering it on a flat export tariff can cause exports that lose money.

settings.friendlyName: Leftover value when export is worthless
settings.description: Discounts end-of-plan battery value when surplus can't be sold for what it cost; the default 0.8 values it at 80% when export pays nothing. 1.0 turns the discount off.
For two or more inverters: rebalances batteries that drift apart or cross-charge by pausing charging or discharging on one.
Balances the batteries' levels while charging (off by default).
Balances the batteries' levels while discharging (off by default).
Stops one inverter's battery charging another in demand mode (on by default).
How far battery levels must differ while charging before balancing starts (default 1%).
How far battery levels must differ while discharging before balancing starts (default 1%).
Merges back-to-back charge slots into one block. Helps stop repeated charge and discharge on long cheap overnight rates; leave off to allow ad-hoc top-ups.
Merges charge or export slots whose prices differ by less than this (pence) into one averaged slot. 0 turns it off.
The smallest saving (pence per kWh) worth charging the battery less for. 0 charges less whenever it is cost-neutral.
0 lets Predbat decide which import prices are cheap enough to charge at. Otherwise a fraction of the average future rate, e.g. 0.8 means 80%.
Charges at the lowest rate that still reaches the target in time; works best on windows longer than one slot. A battery charge curve in apps.yaml is strongly advised.
How many minutes before the window ends low-power charging aims to finish (default 10).

settings.friendlyName: Solar level that cancels low-power charging
settings.description: A charge window whose forecast solar averages above this charges at full rate instead (default 150 W).
Charges at full rate in windows with enough forecast solar, so solar goes into the battery rather than being exported and bought back (on by default).
When charge slots cost the same, prefers the ones with the lowest export price (on by default).
Assumes import prices not yet published (such as Agile before 4pm) are this much higher. Positive values make today's charging more aggressive.
Merges back-to-back export slots into one block. Plans faster, but may prevent the best forced export.
The smallest gain (pence per slot) worth a forced export. Raise it to export only when clearly profitable (default 0.1p).
The smallest gain (pence per slot) worth an export freeze (default 0.1p).
How much extra cost the plan accepts to move an export later in the day; the default -0.25p allows up to 0.25p. Later exports make running out early less likely.
0 lets Predbat decide which export prices are worth exporting at. Otherwise a fraction of the average future export rate, e.g. 1.2 means 20% above.
Lets export slots replace or move charge slots so the two can mix. Off by default.
On (default): forced battery exports can be planned while solar is forecast. Off makes those exports far less attractive.

settings.friendlyName: Keep exports out of cheap import slots
settings.description: When export slots are worth the same, sorts them by import price so exports avoid cheap import times and tend to happen later (on by default).
Tries export freeze on idle sunny slots and keeps it if the plan barely gets worse, so surplus solar is exported instead of stored.
How much the plan may worsen (pence, default 1p) and still keep the extra solar export.
Assumes export prices not yet published are this much different; negative values assume lower prices.
Treats imports as dearer than they are when choosing a plan, so plans with less import win. It only affects which plan is chosen, not reported costs.
Multiplies your past house load to forecast usage. 1.0 uses it as it was; the default 1.05 adds 5%.

settings.friendlyName: Load scaling in the cloudy (PV10) case
settings.description: Extra load factor for the pessimistic PV10% scenario only, on top of house load scaling (default 1.1 adds 10%).

settings.friendlyName: Load scaling in the sunny (PV90) case
settings.description: Load factor for the optimistic PV90% scenario, applied to raw history (default 0.7 means 70%).
Load factor during Octopus saving sessions and Axle export events, to model cutting back (default 1.0).
Load factor during free electricity sessions and Axle import events (default 1.2 adds 20%).
Multiplies the solar forecast. Below 1.0 is more pessimistic; 0.9 removes 10%.
How much the pessimistic 10% solar forecast counts, from 0 to 1 (default 0.15). 0 ignores it.
How much the optimistic 90% solar forecast counts, from 0 to 1 (default 0.15). More weight makes Predbat a little less keen to charge from the grid.
Uses your past generation to correct the solar forecast. Not for Solcast auto-dampening or curtailed exports; needs a Predbat restart to take effect.
Compares today's actual and predicted load and adjusts the rest of today's forecast (on by default).
Scales the in-day load adjustment; lower values soften it (default 0.95).
Varies the solar forecast every 5 minutes to model passing cloud while keeping each half-hour's total (on by default).
Varies the load forecast every 5 minutes based on how much your load usually varies (on by default).
Uses the last 5 minutes of consumption: if load is more than the battery can supply, the plan assumes it continues this slot and avoids forced export.
Drops the lowest-consumption day from the load history when more than one day is used (on by default).
Fraction of normal load assumed for the first day of a holiday, before any holiday history exists (default 0.7).
Uses the PredHeat model to predict your heating system's temperature, energy use and cost.
Turns on carbon footprint tracking; needs a grid CO2 intensity sensor in apps.yaml.
Cost per kg of CO2 used to weigh carbon against money when choosing plans (roughly 10-200).
How often the plan is recalculated (default 10 minutes); the inverter is still controlled every 5 minutes.

settings.friendlyName: Plan length after the first charge
settings.description: Minimum plan length, counted in hours after the first charge slot (24 is recommended).
Re-optimises every charge and export window in time order; slower, sometimes better on Agile (on by default).
Simulates the PV90% upside scenario; turning it off saves planning time (on by default).
Shows the switches that trade planning time for plan quality. While off, those options stay at their defaults.

settings.friendlyName: Minimum improvement for a new plan
Remove car charging from load history
settings.description: Strips past car charging out of the house load history so it doesn't distort the forecast. Turn it off if you have no EV.

settings.friendlyName: Car charger inside the CT clamp
settings.description: On when the charger's energy shows up as house load. Off if it is wired outside the clamp, so the battery can't supply the car.
House load above this power (default 6 kW) is assumed to be car charging, unless a car energy sensor is set in apps.yaml.
Multiplier for the car_charging_energy sensor, e.g. 0.001 to convert W to kW (default 1.0).
The car's charging rate in kW.
Share of energy lost between the house and the car battery when charging (0.08 means 8%).

settings.friendlyName: Enter the car's charge level by hand
settings.description: Ignores the car's charge-level sensor from apps.yaml and uses the level you enter instead.
The car's charge level in kWh that you keep up to date, used when its own sensor is ignored or unavailable.
On: Octopus Intelligent decides when the car charges. Off: Predbat plans car charging itself.
Stops Predbat assuming the car will charge, or that extra cheap slots apply, while it is unplugged. Needs car_charging_planned in apps.yaml.

settings.friendlyName: Stop when the car is full
settings.description: Predicts when the car is full and assumes no more charging after that. Useful when Octopus doesn't know the car's charge level but Predbat does.

settings.friendlyName: Check Intelligent slots against the car
settings.description: Checks each dispatch against whether the car is really charging, and cancels its slots and cheap rate when it isn't (on by default).
On: Intelligent slots are trusted until the car is seen not charging in one. Off: they are ignored until the car is seen charging in one.
Joins Octopus saving sessions automatically as they appear (on by default).

settings.friendlyName: Wait before joining a saving session
settings.description: How many hours before a saving session starts Predbat may join it (default 0 joins straight away).
Uses the cheapest slots before the ready time rather than every low-rate slot in order (on by default).
The most you want to pay per kWh to charge the car (e.g. 10p).

settings.friendlyName: Let the car charge from the battery
settings.description: Off: the home battery won't discharge while the car charges, so the car and house run from the grid. On: the car can drain the home battery.
The time you want the car's charging finished by.
Lets Predbat hold the battery level, running the house from grid and solar, as an alternative to charging (on by default).
Stops the battery charging from the grid; charge freeze can still hold its level. If this is on and charge freeze is off, charge windows can't be used.
Lets Predbat export solar to the grid instead of charging the battery (on by default).
Stops forced battery export; export freeze can still send surplus solar to the grid. For tariffs that pay for solar but don't allow forced export.
For multiple inverters: replaces demand mode with freeze export (the battery can discharge but not charge) to stop cross-charging. Best switched by an automation at sunrise and sunset.
Uses the inverter's reserve setting to hold the battery level or stop it discharging past the limit (on by default).
Disables battery discharge during charge slots, helping multi-inverter systems avoid cross-charging (on by default).
Programs charge slots onto the inverter before they start; off waits until the slot begins (on by default).

settings.friendlyName: Reset the charge target after charging
settings.description: Resets the inverter's charge target to 100% outside charge slots, a workaround for firmware that applies the target to solar charging too (on by default).
Caps the battery charge and discharge rate in watts, e.g. for installs that trip a breaker at full power. 0 means no limit.
Models diverting surplus solar into hot water (iBoost, Eddi or an immersion switch) instead of exporting it.
Assumes the diverter uses solar power to heat water.
On: only solar that would otherwise be exported is diverted. Off (default): any solar can be.
Lets the diverter run while the battery is charging.
Picks the cheapest import slots in the next 24 hours, at or below the price threshold, to deliver the iBoost energy. Only when solar and battery modes are off.
Shortest iBoost run in minutes for the price-only modes (default 30).
Lets iBoost run while the battery is being force-exported.
Stops the battery discharging while iBoost runs. Not recommended with solar diversion, as passing clouds can then cause imports.
Highest import price (pence) at which the diverter runs (default 100).
Highest export price (pence) at which the diverter runs (default 100).

settings.friendlyName: iBoost only when cheaper than gas
settings.description: Runs the diverter only when import electricity is cheaper than gas.

settings.friendlyName: iBoost only when export is below gas
settings.description: Runs the diverter only when the export price is lower than gas.
Scales gas prices for boiler efficiency before comparing them with electricity: 1.25 for an 80% efficient boiler.
The most energy (kWh) the diverter may use in a day (default 3).
The most power (W) the diverter draws (default 2400).
The least power (W) the diverter draws (default 500).
Battery level (%) needed before the diverter turns on (default 0).
What each diverted kWh is worth as a fraction of the lowest future import price (default 0.75); 0 ignores diverted energy.
Subtracts the iboost_energy_today sensor from the load history to improve predictions (on by default).
Predbat's estimate of the diverter's energy use today; resets at midnight.
Notifies you when Predbat's status changes, such as charging or exporting.
Notifies you when inverter settings change, such as rates, reserve or time windows.
Notifies you about energy market events, such as saving sessions joined or Axle events.
Notifies you about system events, such as restarts, software updates and settings save or restore.
Writes extra debug information to the log and a debug file. It turns itself off after 2 hours.
Keeps a rolling history of debug snapshots (on by default).
How many debug snapshots to keep (default 15).
How many hours between automatic debug snapshots (default 3).
Triggers an immediate debug snapshot; Predbat switches it back off afterwards.
Adds extra debug detail to Predbat's own plan table.
Holds every change Predbat's chat agent proposes for your approval before it runs (on by default).
Lets Predbat's chat agent search the web; this costs a little per request (off by default).
Lets Predbat's chat agent read any Home Assistant entity and its history, not just Predbat's (on by default).
On while Predbat's tariff comparison runs; turning it on starts one.
PredHeat's calculated next temperature, used when there is no interior temperature sensor.
Forces charging in the slots you pick, up to 48 hours ahead. Each one is removed once its slot has passed.
Forces export in the slots you pick; this takes priority over manual charging.
Forces normal demand mode (no grid charging or forced export) in the slots you pick.
Holds the battery level in the slots you pick; the grid covers any shortfall.
In the slots you pick the battery won't charge but still runs the house; solar is exported.
Overrides the import price in the slots you pick with the manual import price.
Overrides the export price in the slots you pick with the manual export price.
The price used by manual import prices (default 0p).
The price used by manual export prices (default 0p).
Adds the manual load adjustment to the predicted load in the slots you pick (it can be negative).
The kWh added by manual load adjustments (default 0.5).
Sets a minimum battery level to reach by the times you pick, using the manual target level.
The level (%) used by manual battery targets (default 100).
Sets a maximum battery level by the times you pick, e.g. a calibration discharge before a cheap slot.
The level (%) used by manual battery ceilings. 0% really means empty the battery as far as allowed.
Overrides apps.yaml configuration entries, for example from an automation.
Full days you'll be away, counting today. It counts down at midnight, and holiday mode is on while it is above zero.
Lists Predbat versions you can update or downgrade to. Choosing one installs it.
Updates Predbat automatically when new releases are published.
Saves the current settings to a file, restores the defaults, or restores a saved file.
Shows Predbat's advanced settings. Off by default for new installs.
What Predbat may control: Monitor, Control SoC only, Control charge, or Control charge & discharge. Changing it resets the inverter's settings.
Keeps planning but stops Predbat changing inverter settings. Switching it resets the inverter to its defaults.
